english: For each real number $t>0$, let $m(t)$ denote the minimum value of $x^2+y^2+z^2$ over all real numbers $x,y,z$ satisfying $tx+y+\dfrac4tz=-\dfrac92$. Let $t_0$ be the value of $t$ for which $m(t)$ is greatest, and let $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ be the point at which $x^2+y^2+z^2$ attains the value $m(t_0)$ subject to $t_0x+y+\dfrac4{t_0}z=-\dfrac92$. Then the value of $x_0+y_0+z_0$ is ______.
hindi: प्रत्येक वास्तविक संख्या $t>0$ के लिए माना $m(t)$, $tx+y+\dfrac4tz=-\dfrac92$ को संतुष्ट करने वाली सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x,y,z$ पर $x^2+y^2+z^2$ का न्यूनतम मान है। माना $t_0$, $t$ का वह मान है जिसके लिए $m(t)$ अधिकतम है, तथा $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ वह बिन्दु है जिस पर प्रतिबन्ध $t_0x+y+\dfrac4{t_0}z=-\dfrac92$ के अन्तर्गत $x^2+y^2+z^2$ का मान $m(t_0)$ प्राप्त होता है। तब $x_0+y_0+z_0$ का मान ______ है।
solution: AM-GM: $t^2+\dfrac{16}{t^2}\ge8$, equality iff $t^2=4$; so $m(t)$ is greatest at $t_0=2$ (and $m(2)=\frac94$)
solution_full: Fix $t>0$ and put $\overrightarrow{p}=\left(t,1,\dfrac4t\right)$. The condition says $\overrightarrow p\cdot(x,y,z)=-\dfrac92$.

By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, $\dfrac{81}{4}\le|\overrightarrow p|^2(x^2+y^2+z^2)$, with equality iff $(x,y,z)$ is a multiple of $\overrightarrow p$. So $m(t)=\dfrac{81}{4\left(t^2+1+\frac{16}{t^2}\right)}$, attained only at $(x,y,z)=\lambda\overrightarrow p$ with $\lambda=-\dfrac{9}{2|\overrightarrow p|^2}$.

$m(t)$ is greatest when $t^2+\dfrac{16}{t^2}$ is least. By AM-GM, $t^2+\dfrac{16}{t^2}\ge2\sqrt{16}=8$, with equality iff $t^2=4$, i.e. $t=2$ (as $t>0$). So $t_0=2$ and $m(t_0)=\dfrac{81}{4\cdot9}=\dfrac94$.
originality_note: New: a one-parameter family of planes whose distance from the origin is maximised over the parameter; Cauchy-Schwarz gives the inner minimum and AM-GM the outer maximum, and the answer is read off the extremal point (way 5: Cauchy-Schwarz nested inside an AM-GM extremum). Closest known: 'minimum of x^2 + y^2 + z^2 subject to ax + by + cz = d' (distance to a plane). Different because: the coefficients depend on t, so a second optimisation over t is needed before the point is found.
blueprint_concepts: Arithmetic Mean (AM), Geometric Mean (GM) & AM-GM Inequality: maximising / minimising expressions under a constraint
Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality: Application in algebraic extrema.

concept_use.Arithmetic Mean (AM), Geometric Mean (GM: AM-GM on t^2 + 16/t^2 >= 8 decides where m(t) is greatest (t_0 = 2).
